title: Visual Literacy: Advertisements and Cartoons
summary: Reading visual texts: layout, images, colour, font, slogans and target audience in advertisements, and frames, speech bubbles and humour in cartoons.

rows: Grabs attention, often with a pun or question
Shows the product or creates a mood
A memorable phrase linked to the brand
Tells the reader what to do: 'Order now!'

notes.title: Naming the parts
notes.problem: An advert has 'Run Further' in large letters, a picture of shoes and small text saying 'Available at all sports shops'. Name the parts.
steps: The largest attention-grabbing words are the headline.
The picture is the main visual.
The small information is body copy.

items: **Colour**: green suggests nature and health; red suggests energy, danger or passion; gold suggests luxury.
**Font**: bold capitals for urgency; elegant script for luxury.
**Layout**: the eye is drawn to the largest or brightest item first.
**Target audience**: who the advert is aimed at, shown by images, language and the product.

notes.title: Described advertisement (original)
notes.text: A smiling teenager in a soccer kit drinks from a bright green bottle. Water droplets sparkle on the bottle. HEADLINE (large white capitals): 'GAME ON!' BODY COPY: 'Fuel up with ZEST Sports Water: zero sugar, all-natural lemon flavour, and the electrolytes your body needs.' SLOGAN (bottom right, beside a lightning-bolt logo): 'ZEST. Feel the charge.'

Cartoons use **frames**, **speech bubbles** (words), **thought bubbles** (thoughts), **facial expressions**, **body language** and **exaggeration**. Humour often comes from **irony**, **puns** or a surprising **punchline** in the last frame.

notes.label: Exam tip
notes.text: Describe what you see, then explain its effect: 'The teenager's broad smile suggests the drink makes you feel happy and energetic.'

notes.title: Explaining a cartoon
notes.problem: A cartoon shows a politician promising 'Clean water for all' while standing on a dry tap. What is its point?
steps: Identify the contrast between the words and the image.
notes.answer: It criticises politicians for empty promises.

questions.prompt: Quote the slogan of the ZEST advertisement.
Who is the most likely target audience of the ZEST advertisement?
What does the green colour of the bottle most likely suggest?
'Order now!' is an example of a call to action.
Speech bubbles in cartoons show what characters are thinking but not saying.
Match each ZEST element to its type.
Explain why 'GAME ON!' is an effective headline.
questions.memo:
✓ It is short, bold and energetic (1)
✓ and links the drink to sport/excitement, appealing to the target audience (1)

questions.prompt: Explain the double meaning of 'Feel the charge'.
questions.memo:
✓ 'Charge' means energy/electrical charge (linked to the lightning bolt and electrolytes) (1)
✓ and to charge forward/attack in a game (1)

questions.prompt: Why does the designer show water droplets on the bottle?
questions.memo:
✓ They suggest the drink is cold (1)
✓ and refreshing, making it more appealing (1)

questions.prompt: Do you think the advertisement is convincing? Give ONE reason.
questions.memo:
✓ Clear opinion (1)
✓ Supported reason from the visual or text (1)
